name: International Protection (Refugee Status / Subsidiary Protection)

requirements.blocker_text: Law No. 06/L-026 on Asylum, Article 49(1): the Department for Citizenship, Asylum and Migration (DCAM) decides applications for international protection at first instance; appeals go to the National Commission for Refugees (Article 49(2)) within 14 days (Article 73(1)), with further recourse to the competent courts (Article 73(2)). Applications are lodged at border crossings, police stations, or DCAM offices (Article 52(1)) and must be registered within 3-6 working days (Article 52(6-7)); applicants are informed of their rights and the procedure within 15 days (Article 12(2)). First-instance decisions are due within 6 months, extendable to 9 months for complex cases or a mass influx (Article 72). Recognized beneficiaries (Article 35(1)) get residence rights (Article 36), employment WITHOUT needing a separate work permit (Article 43(1)), family reunification (Article 44), equal access to education and healthcare, and property ownership rights (Article 46).
requirements.fix_path: Lodge the application at a border crossing, police station, or DCAM office; a first-instance decision is due within 6-9 months, with a 14-day window to appeal to the National Commission for Refugees.

outcome.duration_length: indefinite, tied to continued protection needs

sources.title: Refworld (hosted primary legal text) -- Law No. 06/L-026 on Asylum, Articles 12, 35-36, 43-46, 49, 52, 72-73

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Kosovo). STATUS: DRAFT -- sourced to Refworld's hosted copy of the primary legal text, tier 2 (not tier 1 despite being Kosovo's own law, since the hosting party is Refworld/UNHCR rather than a .rks-gov.net domain -- Kosovo's own Official Gazette almost certainly hosts this law too, but was not independently fetched in this build for the asylum text specifically). GENUINE, POSITIVE FINDING: this is one of the MOST fully fleshed-out humanitarian-protection files in this entire dataset -- a named first-instance body (DCAM) and a separate appeals body (National Commission for Refugees), concrete registration and decision timelines, an explicit appeal window, and unusually generous confirmed refugee rights (employment WITHOUT a separate work permit, family reunification, property ownership) -- a sharp contrast with Algeria and Haiti (both built earlier in this dataset), where no domestic asylum framework exists at all. work_rights and study_rights set to 'full' directly per Article 35/43, a rare case in this dataset where those fields are confidently sourced rather than defaulted conservatively.
